generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science, revising on purpose means planning around the topics you find hardest, perhaps biomechanics or a physiology pathway, not just the ones you like. You test yourself to find the gaps, revise them actively, and pick a technique that fits, such as acting out a movement sequence. Each round shows what still needs work, so you adjust and go again.
generatedProse.worked-example: Marcus is revising a sport science module with biomechanics, a set of anatomy terms, and a physiology pathway with many linked stages. At first he plans to re-read his notes for equal time. Instead he tests himself, finds biomechanics is his weakest area, and gives it the most time. He drills the anatomy terms with flashcards, walks through the physiology pathway as a kinaesthetic sequence, and works biomechanics problems actively. By the exam he is strongest where he was once weakest.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, revising on purpose means running the three ideas together across the module. You plan around your weak topics, revise them actively, and choose a technique that fits each one, from flashcards for terms to a walk-through for a pathway. Repeated and adjusted, that practice is what readies you for the exam.

check.body: A student lists her topics, tests herself to find the weak ones, gives them the most time, and revises each with a technique chosen to fit it. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: One revision practice at work: a strategy built on time and gaps, filled with active revision and techniques that fit the material.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three ideas are running together as one practice.

_items.text: That she is spending too long on revision and should cut it down.
_items.feedback: The point is not how long she spends. It is that the three ideas work together.

_items.text: That the technique she picks is the only thing that matters.
